model: HMI-VOLCANO EC controller for VOLCANO air heaters
applies_to: VTS HMI-VOLCANO EC wall controller with Modbus RTU, device integration manual version 1.1.
summary: The HMI-VOLCANO EC is the room controller for VTS VOLCANO EC fan heaters, which can run in heating or cooling mode. Over Modbus RTU a BMS can switch it on and off, choose heating or cooling, set the fan output and room setpoint, edit the weekly schedule and read the room temperature, schedule state and output states.

addressing.note: Every table gives the address 'for PDU' in decimal and hex (first register 0 = 0x0000), so that address goes on the wire unchanged. The function-code examples count registers from 1 instead (register 108 is requested as 0x006B = 107), which matches: PDU address = register number - 1. This map uses the 'for PDU' column.

source.title: HMI-VOLCANO EC - Device Integration Manual on Modbus RTU Bus
source.pages: pp. 2-7 function codes and examples, pp. 8-19 holding registers (table 14) and their meaning, p. 20 input registers, p. 21 discrete inputs, pp. 22-24 coils and default values

notes: Holding registers 0-3 (baud, parity, address, sensor correction) must be written one per message; a multi-register write that includes them is refused.
Temperatures are in 0.01 °C (value / 100). When the controller is set to °F, temperature registers are in °F with the same scale.
Left out: coils 5 and 6 (temperature unit and clock format) and holding register 40 (fan regulation mode), which appear only in the default-value table and not in the register tables.
Defaults per the default-value table: 9600 baud (960), even parity, address 1, setpoint 22.00 °C, ECO 18.00 °C.

integration.summary: Switch the unit with coil 2, select heating/cooling with holding 21, set the room setpoint (0.01 °C) in holding 23 and fan output % in holding 22; read the room temperature from input register 0.
integration.enable: Modbus RTU is always active on the RS485 terminals (J3 A/B); change baud, parity and address through holding registers 0-2 (the device restarts after each change).
quirks: Setpoints are rounded to 0.5 °C and schedule times to 15 minutes.
Parity is written as the ASCII code of 'e', 'o' or 'n'; 'n' uses 2 stop bits.
Writing a setpoint below MIN or above MAX is refused.
setup: RS485 on terminal block J3 (A, B, ground).
gotchas: A sensor fault reads -32768 (shown as 327.68 when treated as unsigned).

address_note: address = 0-based Modbus wire (PDU) address; documented = as printed in the source.
